scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being a "nass" (which I think is slang for "nervous" or maybe "nasty," but not sure) in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, my wife and I didn't do a lot of traditional wedding things. That's cool because we wanted to keep it simple and personal. One thing she really wanted was for me not to see her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed to that because it was important to her, and I wanted to make her happy. On the day of the wedding, she looked beautiful, as always. But honestly, I didn't think the dress was flattering. I mean, I know she loved it, and her best friend kept showing me those reaction posts of grooms crying when they see their brides. They even tagged me, saying that would be my reaction. But when the day came, I didn't cry or get overly emotional. I smiled, focused on her, and we got married. The reception went fine, and our honeymoon was great. After the honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend, who mentioned that I had an underwhelming reaction. She showed me pictures where I didn't look as emotional as she expected. I told her I didn't realize that, and she said she didn't want me to cry but just thought I would be more emotional because it was such a big day. I explained that I was ecstatic to marry her, and that showed without being overly dramatic. I also mentioned that her friend was nudging me the whole time, which felt unfair. Finally, I asked if we had a wedding or a play because I never got any "lines" to follow. Now she's mad at me, and I feel bad because she's disappointed, but I couldn't force myself to have that reaction. So, am I being a nass here? I don't think so. I was honest about my feelings, and I made an effort to make the day special for her. I didn't hide my emotions, but I also didn't feel the need to cry or overreact. I think it's okay to have different ways of showing love and happiness. Maybe she expected a certain reaction because of societal norms or what she saw online, but that doesn't mean it's the only way to feel or express love. I also think it's important to communicate openly. I told her how I felt, and I explained why I reacted the way I did. It's not about being right or wrong, but about understanding each other's perspectives. Maybe she felt let down because she wanted that moment to be special, and my reaction didn't match her expectations. But I was there, I supported her, and we had a beautiful day together. In the end, I don't think I'm being a nass. I was genuine, honest, and present. It's tough when someone's expectations don't align with reality, but that doesn't make me a bad person. I just hope we can talk about it and move forward together.
